- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.05) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.3) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust for recent sentiment shifts or price momentum.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model overreacts and forecasts higher prices for 2–5 days — apply downward correction after peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high in consolidation zones — reduce forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent highs — use 18-day history as anchor for smoothing, not 30-day trend.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.05), model drifts toward historical mean — avoid extrapolation; use recent 7-day average for calibration.
